_note: 术语表：由重构者编写。每个词条给出所属章节、一句话定义与一个「为什么」（为什么这个概念重要 / 容易搞错的地方）。

terms.zh_def: 把「数据 → 信息 → 知识 → 智慧」四级串起来的层次模型。数据是原始观察，信息是组织过的数据，知识是从信息里提炼出的规律，智慧是据知识做判断。
terms.zh_why: 可视化的能力边界就在这里：它主要把数据升到信息，少数场景能到知识，跨不到智慧。分不清这一层，就很容易承诺可视化做不到的事。
terms.en_def: A four-level hierarchy: data → information → knowledge → wisdom. Data are raw observations, information is data that has been organised, knowledge is the regularities distilled from information, and wisdom is judgement built on that knowledge.
terms.en_why: This is exactly where visualization runs out of road: it mostly lifts data to information, occasionally reaches knowledge, and never crosses into wisdom. Confuse the levels and you end up promising something a chart cannot deliver.

terms.zh_def: Stevens 四种测量尺度里最弱的一种：只允许判断相等或不等，没有任何顺序。姓名、性别都属于这一类。
terms.zh_why: 名义数据只能用色相、形状这类定性通道编码 —— 给性别做平均值是没有意义的。
terms.en_def: The weakest of Stevens' four measurement scales: values can only be tested for equality or difference, with no order at all. Names and gender fall into this class.
terms.en_why: Nominal data can only be encoded on qualitative channels such as hue and shape — averaging gender is meaningless, and so is a line chart that implies an order between categories.

terms.zh_def: 值之间有顺序，但相邻两级的差不一定相等。学历（本科 / 硕士 / 博士）是典型例子。
terms.zh_why: 差不一定相等，所以序数数据很适合用亮度、饱和度这类顺序通道，而不适合用位置。
terms.en_def: Values have an order, but the gaps between adjacent levels need not be equal. Education level (bachelor / master / doctorate) is the classic example.
terms.en_why: Because the gaps are unequal, ordinal data suits ordered channels such as lightness and saturation, and is a poor fit for position — a position axis invites readers to measure distances that mean nothing.

terms.zh_def: 区间尺度支持加减（摄氏温度），比率尺度还支持乘除（年龄、价格）。唯一的区别是有没有「真零点」。
terms.zh_why: 0°C 不等于没有温度，所以不能说 20°C 是 10°C 的两倍；0 元才等于没有钱。这条决定了什么时候可以算比值。
terms.en_def: Interval scales support addition and subtraction (Celsius temperature); ratio scales additionally support multiplication and division (age, price). The only difference is whether there is a true zero.
terms.en_why: 0 °C does not mean 'no temperature', so 20 °C is not twice as warm as 10 °C; 0 yuan does mean 'no money'. This decides when a ratio is meaningful — and when a bar chart lies by starting from a fake zero.

terms.zh_def: 承载数据变化的视觉属性，位置、长度、角度、面积、亮度、饱和度、色相、形状、纹理等。
terms.zh_why: Mackinlay 把通道按表达能力排了序：位置最能表达定量，色相最能表达定性。属性与通道配错，信息就会丢。
terms.en_def: A visual property that can carry variation in data: position, length, angle, area, brightness, saturation, hue, shape, texture.
terms.en_why: Mackinlay ranked channels by how much they can express: position is the strongest for quantitative values, hue the strongest for categories. Pair an attribute with the wrong channel and information is lost — a pie chart is exactly that mistake.

terms.zh_def: 把数据数组绑定到 DOM 元素时出现的三种情况：元素不够是 enter，正好是 update，多了是 exit。
terms.zh_why: 这是 D3 的核心心智模型。理解了它，D3 就从「一堆 API」变成「一条数据到画面的映射」。
terms.en_def: Binding an array of data to DOM elements produces three cases: too few elements is enter, an exact match is update, surplus elements is exit.
terms.en_why: This is the core mental model of D3. Once you have it, D3 stops being a pile of APIs and becomes one mapping from data to pixels; without it, every selection method feels arbitrary.

terms.zh_def: 在绑定数据时告诉 D3「哪个数据对应哪个元素」的函数，通常写成 d => d.id。
terms.zh_why: 没有 key，D3 按数组下标认身份：数据一重排，所有元素都算「变过」，过渡动画就乱了。有 key，元素才知道自己是谁。
terms.en_def: A function that tells D3 which data item belongs to which element when binding, usually written d => d.id.
terms.en_why: Without a key, D3 identifies elements by array index: reorder the data and every element counts as changed, so transitions scramble. With a key, each element knows who it is and animates from its own previous state.

terms.zh_def: 把可视化拆成四步：原数据 → 数据表 → 视觉结构 → 视图。1999 年由 Stuart Card 提出。
terms.zh_why: 它是整门课的骨架。有了这套坐标系，遇到任何一张陌生的图，你都能问「它在哪一步做了什么处理」。
terms.en_def: Stuart Card's 1999 model splits visualization into four stages: raw data → data tables → visual structures → views.
terms.en_why: It is the skeleton of this whole course. With that frame you can meet any unfamiliar chart and ask what it did at each stage — what was filtered, what was encoded, what was drawn.

terms.zh_def: 按给定键分组，并对每组算出一个聚合值，返回 Map。和 d3.group 的区别是它只留聚合结果。
terms.zh_why: 把平表变成层次结构最实用的一步。树形图、分组柱状图的上游数据几乎都是它生成的。
terms.en_def: Group by the given key and reduce each group to a single value, returning a Map. Unlike d3.group, it keeps only the aggregate.
terms.en_why: It is the most practical single step from a flat table to a hierarchy: treemaps, grouped bars and stacked areas almost always start from a d3.rollup call.

terms.zh_def: 一种经典树状图布局算法，让同层节点均匀铺开，同时父节点尽量居中于其子节点之上。
terms.zh_why: 手写树布局很容易左右不平衡、线条交叉。这个算法把「看起来舒服」这件事变成了可计算的规则。
terms.en_def: A classic tree layout that spreads siblings evenly across the available width while keeping each parent centred over its children.
terms.en_why: Hand-rolled tree layouts drift out of balance and cross their own edges. This algorithm turns 'looks tidy' into a computable rule, which is why d3.tree() still implements it.

terms.zh_def: 把监听器绑在父元素上，靠事件冒泡统一处理所有子元素的事件。
terms.zh_why: 元素数量成千上万时，给每个元素单独绑监听器的开销会线性上涨。委托只有一个监听器，而且动态增删的子元素也能自动接管。
terms.en_def: Attach one listener to a parent element and let events bubble up from its children, handling them all in one place.
terms.en_why: With thousands of elements, per-element listeners grow linearly and leak as elements come and go. One delegated listener stays flat — and children added later are handled automatically.

terms.zh_def: 描述颜色的坐标系。RGB 面向屏幕，HSL 面向直觉，Lab / HCL 面向感知。
terms.zh_why: 做数据映射必须用感知均匀的空间：在 RGB 里等距离的两个颜色，人眼看着并不等距，映射出来的图会骗人。
terms.en_def: A coordinate system for describing colour: RGB is built for screens, HSL for intuition, Lab and HCL for perception.
terms.en_why: Mapping data to colour demands a perceptually uniform space. Two colours the same distance apart in RGB are not the same distance apart to the eye, so a colormap built in RGB will lie about magnitude.

terms.zh_def: 顺序型（数值单调变化）、发散型（有一个有意义的中间值）、定性型（类别之间无顺序）。
terms.zh_why: 选错类型的代价很大：给没有中心的数据用发散型，读者会读出一个不存在的中心；给类别数据用顺序型，读者会以为类别能比大小。
terms.en_def: Sequential (a value rises monotonically), diverging (a meaningful midpoint) and qualitative (categories with no order).
terms.en_why: Getting the type wrong is expensive: a diverging map on data without a centre invents one, and a sequential map on categories makes readers think the categories can be ranked.

terms.zh_def: 红绿色盲、蓝黄色盲等色觉差异。男性中红绿色盲比例约为 8%。
terms.zh_why: 只靠色相区分数据，意味着约每十二个男性读者里就有一个读不了你的图。这是把「可读性」变成硬指标的少数几处之一。
terms.en_def: Colour-vision deficiencies such as protanopia and deuteranopia (red–green) or tritanopia (blue–yellow). Around 8% of men are red–green colour-blind.
terms.en_why: Encoding data by hue alone means roughly one in twelve male readers cannot read your chart. This is one of the few places where accessibility becomes a hard, checkable requirement.

terms.zh_def: 发表在 Nature Methods (2011) 的一组定性色板，经过色觉缺陷友好性与等亮度检验。
terms.zh_why: 本网站自身的配色也取自这套色板 —— 课程讲的配色原则，在课程网站自己身上先用一遍。
terms.en_def: A qualitative palette published in Nature Methods (2011), tested both for colour-vision deficiency and for even lightness.
terms.en_why: This site's own palette comes from it: the principles the course teaches are applied to the course site itself, so the lessons and the medium agree.

terms.zh_def: 一类配色策略：保色相上的区分度（鲜艳），同时压低饱和度（不刺眼），并把颜色数量控制在 7 个以内。
terms.zh_why: 高饱和多色最大的问题不是丑，是「吵」—— 每一块颜色都在抢注意力，读者反而找不到重点。
terms.en_def: A palette strategy that keeps hue separation (vivid) while pushing saturation down (easy on the eye), with the number of colours capped around seven.
terms.en_why: The problem with many saturated colours is not ugliness but noise: every patch competes for attention, so the reader finds no focus. Lower saturation lets one accent do the pointing.

terms.zh_def: 数据空间（语义）→ 坐标系空间（几何）→ 屏幕空间（像素）。每一层只负责一件事。
terms.zh_why: 初学者常把这三种变换揉在一起写，于是改一处就崩一片。分层之后，比例尺该做什么、什么不该做，就清楚了。
terms.en_def: Data space (meaning) → coordinate space (geometry) → screen space (pixels). Each layer does exactly one job.
terms.en_why: Beginners fold the three transforms into one expression, so a change in one breaks the rest. Kept apart, it becomes obvious what a scale should do — and what it should never do.

terms.zh_def: 人眼对斜率的估计在 45° 附近最准确（也称 banking to 45°）。
terms.zh_why: 它把「图表该多宽多高」从审美问题变成了感知问题：想让人准确比较趋势，就把主要趋势线摆到 45° 附近。
terms.en_def: The eye estimates slopes most accurately near 45°, a result known as banking to 45°.
terms.en_why: It turns aspect ratio from a question of taste into a question of perception: if readers must compare trends, put the dominant trend near 45° instead of arguing about how tall the chart should be.

terms.zh_def: 在规则网格上逐格判断四角与阈值的关系，生成等值线段，再拼接成完整等值线的算法。
terms.zh_why: 它是等值线图和热力图平滑化的底层。难点不在循环，而在「四角两两高于阈值」时的歧义格子 —— 连线方式不同，结果形状会不一样。
terms.en_def: A grid algorithm that tests each cell's four corners against a threshold and stitches the resulting segments into full contour lines.
terms.en_why: It underlies contour plots and smoothed heatmaps. The difficulty is not the loop but the ambiguous cells where two corners are above the threshold and two below — different resolutions give different shapes.

terms.zh_def: 有序、连续、周期、独立于空间、有结构（间隔有含义）。
terms.zh_why: 其中「独立于空间」这一条最关键：空间数据的位置自带信息，时间必须由你决定它怎么落到平面上，所以时间可视化才有这么多非标准布局。
terms.en_def: Ordered, continuous, cyclic, independent of space, and structured (intervals carry meaning).
terms.en_why: 'Independent of space' matters most: spatial position carries its own information, but time has no position until you choose one — which is why time visualization has so many non-standard layouts.

terms.zh_def: 把一年按「行 = 年 / 列 = 周」摆成网格，用颜色表示每天的值。
terms.zh_why: 它牺牲了精确的数值比较，换来整年的模式识别 —— 这是布局设计里典型的「用精度换结构」。
terms.en_def: A calendar grid with years as rows and weeks as columns, colouring each day by its value.
terms.en_why: It gives up precise value comparison in exchange for pattern recognition across a whole year — the classic 'trade precision for structure' move in layout design.

terms.zh_def: 半径随角度线性增长的螺旋线。把时间沿它排列，同一周期的数据会落在同一条辐射方向上。
terms.zh_why: 折线图会把周期切成碎片，螺旋则让周期对齐成径向的一条条 —— 周期性因此变得可以直接看出来。
terms.en_def: A spiral whose radius grows linearly with angle. Laying time along it makes data from the same phase of each cycle fall on the same ray.
terms.en_why: A line chart chops a cycle into fragments; a spiral aligns the cycles into radial spokes, so periodicity becomes visible at a glance.

terms.zh_def: 多角色叙事可视化：每条线代表一个角色、组织或进程，线的交叉表示它们相遇或产生关系。
terms.zh_why: 它是少数几个能把「叙事结构」本身画出来的方法。《侏罗纪公园》案例里，角色线的交织就是剧情的结构。
terms.en_def: A narrative visualization in which each line is a character, organisation or process, and crossings mark encounters or relationships.
terms.en_why: It is one of the few methods that draws narrative structure itself. In the Jurassic Park case, the interweaving of the character lines is the plot.

terms.zh_def: 把数据域映射到值域的函数。连续量用 scaleLinear，离散分类用 scaleBand，序数可用 scalePoint。
terms.zh_why: 选错比例尺是最常见的新手错误：给类别数据用线性比例尺，会算出「0.5 班」这种没有意义的值。
terms.en_def: A function mapping a data domain to a visual range. Continuous values use scaleLinear, ordered categories use scaleBand, and points on a category axis use scalePoint.
terms.en_why: Picking the wrong scale is the most common beginner error: a linear scale on categorical data produces meaningless values such as '0.5 of a class'.

terms.zh_def: colormap 是连续的（可插值），用于数值映射；色板是离散的一组颜色，用于类别区分。
terms.zh_why: 把连续的 colormap 用在类别数据上，会暗示类别之间有中间态；把离散色板用在数值上，则会让读者以为数据是分档的。
terms.en_def: A colormap is continuous and interpolated, used to map values; a palette is a discrete set of colours, used to separate categories.
terms.en_why: A continuous colormap on categorical data implies states in between; a discrete palette on continuous values implies the data is binned. Neither claim is true, and both mislead.
